nodes.name: ⏰ Schedule Trigger (Weekdays 9am)
nodes.notes:
Triggers the full pipeline automatically every weekday at 9am.
Can also be replaced with a Manual Trigger for on-demand runs.
Configurable: change cronExpression for different schedules.

nodes.name: ⚙️ Init: Session Config
nodes.notes:
Initialises batch session configuration.
Defines: search query, location, radius, pagination depth.
Defines: company profile used by AI lead scorer.
Creates unique batchId for tracking.

To customise:
- Change searchQuery to your target niche
- Change location to your target market
- Adjust targetIndustries for your ICP (Ideal Customer Profile)

nodes.name: 🔍 Google Places: Text Search (Page 1)
nodes.notes:
Calls Google Places Text Search API to get the first page of results.
Returns up to 20 places with: place_id, name, formatted_address, rating,
user_ratings_total, types, geometry.

API Key: Set GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY in n8n environment variables.
Billing: Google Places API — $17 per 1000 requests (Text Search).

Response includes next_page_token if more results exist.

nodes.name: 📋 Extract Page 1 Results
nodes.notes:
Extracts results from Page 1 response.
Checks API status — throws error on INVALID_REQUEST / OVER_QUERY_LIMIT.
Stores next_page_token for pagination loop.
Merges with session config for downstream nodes.

nodes.name: 🔀 IF: More Pages?
nodes.notes:
Controls pagination loop.
Continues ONLY if:
  1. next_page_token exists (API returned more results)
  2. current page is below maxPages limit

TRUE  → Fetch next page
FALSE → Proceed to place detail fetching

nodes.name: ⏱️ Wait 2s (Rate Limit)
nodes.notes:
Google Places API requires a 2-second delay between paginated requests.
The next_page_token is not valid immediately — Google needs time to generate it.
Without this wait, the API returns INVALID_REQUEST.

This is documented in Google's Places API pagination requirements.

nodes.name: 🔍 Google Places: Next Page
nodes.notes:
Fetches next page of Google Places results using next_page_token.
Only uses pagetoken parameter — no other search params needed.
Returns another 20 results and possibly another next_page_token.

This node feeds back into the pagination check (loop).

nodes.name: 🔗 Merge Page Results
nodes.notes:
Accumulates results across all pages into a single allPlaces array.
Updates currentPage counter and checks for further pagination.
Loops back to IF node for next page check.

Final output: allPlaces[] containing all scraped place summaries.

nodes.name: ✂️ Split: Individual Places
nodes.notes:
Splits the accumulated allPlaces array into individual n8n items.
Each downstream node now processes ONE place at a time.

Attaches session metadata (batchId, ourCompany profile) to each item
so AI scoring node has company context without re-querying.

Output: N items (one per place found)

nodes.name: 📍 Google Places: Fetch Details
nodes.notes:
Fetches detailed information for each place using its place_id.

Fields requested:
- formatted_phone_number: direct contact
- website: for email extraction
- rating + user_ratings_total: quality signal
- opening_hours: operational status
- price_level: budget indicator (1-4)
- editorial_summary: AI-generated description
- reviews: sentiment data (first 5 reviews)

API Cost: ~$0.017 per Details request.
Billing: Set quota alerts in Google Cloud Console.

nodes.name: 🔧 Parse Place Details
nodes.notes:
Merges Places Details API response with base place data.
Extracts: phone, website, hours, price level, reviews.
Maps price_level integer to readable label.
Sets hasWebsite and hasPhone booleans for AI scoring.
Initialises email field as empty string for next node.

nodes.name: 🔀 IF: Has Website?
nodes.notes:
Routes places WITH a website to email extraction.
Places WITHOUT a website skip directly to AI scoring
(they will have email='' but still receive an AI score).

This prevents unnecessary HTTP requests for websiteless businesses.

nodes.name: 🌐 Fetch Website HTML
nodes.notes:
Fetches the HTML of the business website for email extraction.

continueOnFail: true — if website is unreachable (404, timeout, SSL error),
workflow continues with email='' rather than crashing.

Timeout: 15 seconds — long enough for slow sites.
Follows redirects: up to 5 (handles http→https, www→non-www).
Returns raw HTML text for regex parsing.

nodes.name: 📧 Extract Email from HTML
nodes.notes:
Extracts email addresses from website HTML using regex.

Priority order:
1. info@ / contact@ / sales@ / hello@ (most valuable)
2. Any other business email found
3. Empty string if none found

Filters out:
- Known platform domains (Wix, WordPress, Shopify CDN emails)
- Image/asset file references that look like emails
- Emails over 80 characters (likely data URLs)

Deduplicates using Set before filtering.

nodes.name: ⬜ No Website — Pass Through
nodes.notes:
Handles businesses without a website URL.
Passes data through unchanged with email='' and emailExtracted=false.
Ensures all items have identical structure before reaching AI scoring.

nodes.name: 🔀 Merge Paths → Pre-AI
nodes.notes:
Convergence node — merges both website and no-website paths.
Ensures every item has identical field structure before AI scoring.
Sets default values for all fields that may be missing.
Initialises aiScore=null, aiTier='', aiReasoning='' as placeholders.

values.content:
You are a B2B sales lead qualification specialist. Your job is to score business leads for outreach potential.

You MUST respond with ONLY a valid JSON object — no markdown, no explanation, no preamble. Exactly this structure:
{
  "score": <integer 1-10>,
  "tier": <"Hot" | "Warm" | "Cold">,
  "reasoning": "<2-3 sentence explanation>",
  "topStrength": "<single best qualifying factor>",
  "topWeakness": "<single biggest gap or concern>",
  "recommendedAction": "<one concrete next step>"
}

Scoring criteria:
- Rating 4.0+: +2 points
- Rating 3.5-3.9: +1 point
- 50+ reviews: +1 point, 100+ reviews: +2 points
- Has email: +2 points
- Has website: +1 point
- Has phone: +1 point
- Industry match: +1-2 points
- OPERATIONAL business status: +1 point
- Editorial summary available: +0.5 points

Tier thresholds:
- Hot: score 8-10
- Warm: score 5-7
- Cold: score 1-4

nodes.name: 🤖 AI: Score Lead (GPT-4o-mini)
nodes.notes:
★ CORE AI NODE — Lead Qualification Scoring

Model: GPT-4o-mini
- Cost-efficient: ~$0.00015 per lead scored
- Temperature: 0.2 (deterministic, consistent scoring)
- MaxTokens: 600 (enough for full JSON response)

Prompt design:
- System prompt defines exact scoring criteria
- User prompt injects all lead data dynamically
- Forces JSON-only output (no markdown wrappers)

Output fields:
- score: 1-10 integer
- tier: Hot / Warm / Cold
- reasoning: 2-3 sentence explanation
- topStrength: best qualifying factor
- topWeakness: biggest gap/concern
- recommendedAction: concrete next step

Business context:
- Passes ourCompany profile so AI knows ICP
- Matching industry types boost score
- Missing email/website reduces score

nodes.name: 🔧 Parse AI Score
nodes.notes:
Safely parses the AI scoring response.

Fallback handling:
1. Primary: JSON.parse() after stripping markdown fences
2. Fallback: regex extraction of score and tier values
3. Last resort: score=5, tier=Warm, reasoning='parsing failed'

Validation:
- Clamps score between 1-10 (prevents out-of-range values)
- Validates tier is one of Hot/Warm/Cold
- Calculates tier from score if AI tier is invalid

Output: lead data + all AI scoring fields ready for Sheets.

nodes.name: 📊 Google Sheets: Write Lead + Score
nodes.notes:
Writes the complete enriched lead row to Google Sheets.

Operation: appendOrUpdate
- Match key: Place ID (prevents duplicates on re-run)
- If Place ID exists → updates that row
- If new Place ID → appends new row

24 columns written per lead:
Batch ID | Place ID | Name | Address | Phone | Website | Email |
Rating | Reviews | Types | Price | Status | Description |
AI Score | AI Tier | AI Reasoning | Top Strength | Top Weakness |
Recommended Action | Has Email | Has Website | Has Phone |
Scored At | Score Source

Sheet must have these headers in Row 1 of 'Leads' tab.

nodes.name: 📈 Aggregate Batch Summary
nodes.notes:
Aggregates statistics across ALL processed leads in the batch.

Computes:
- Total leads processed
- Hot / Warm / Cold distribution
- Count with email found
- Count with website
- Average AI score
- Top 5 highest-scored leads (for Telegram summary)

This node waits for ALL items before executing (n8n aggregation behavior).
Passes the summary forward to the Telegram notification node.

nodes.name: 📝 Build Telegram Message
nodes.notes:
Constructs the admin Telegram notification message.

Message includes:
- Batch ID and completion timestamp
- Formatted table: total / hot / warm / cold / email / website / avg score
- Top 5 highest-scored leads with:
  - Business name, score, tier
  - Email and phone
  - AI-recommended action
- Direct link to Google Sheet

Uses Telegram Markdown formatting:
- *bold* for headers
- `code` for batch ID
- Emoji indicators for each metric

nodes.name: 📱 Telegram: Admin Notification
nodes.notes:
★ ADMIN NOTIFICATION — Task B Deliverable

Sends the batch completion summary to the admin via Telegram.

Setup:
1. Create a bot via @BotFather on Telegram
2. Copy the Bot Token to n8n Credentials → Telegram API
3. Get your Chat ID from @userinfobot
4. Set TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID in n8n environment variables

Alternative (Slack):
- Replace this node with n8n-nodes-base.slack
- Use 'Send Message' operation
- Set channel: #sales-leads
- Pass telegramMessage as the text

Notification is AUDIBLE (disable_notification: false)
because batch completion is an important business event.

nodes.name: 📊 Sheets: Log Batch Summary
nodes.notes:
Logs a batch-level summary row to the 'BatchLog' sheet tab.
Provides a historical audit trail of every scraping run.

BatchLog columns:
Batch ID | Completed At | Total Leads | Hot | Warm | Cold |
With Email | With Website | Avg AI Score | Status

Status is hardcoded 'SUCCESS' here.
The Error Trigger workflow writes 'ERROR' status for failed batches.
